units.function: Monolithic plugin I/O orchestrator for filesystem/npm discovery, local builds, manifest loading, install and upgrade persistence, database migrations, worker activation, config replay, jobs, events, webhooks, tools and shutdown.
units.dependencyDirection: Directly couples server, database, shared manifest/record types, SDK error codes, npm/pnpm/filesystem/process execution and every plugin runtime subsystem; callers depend on a broad service interface with optional runtime mode.
units.keyDataModels: DiscoveredPlugin, PluginInstallOptions, PluginRecord/manifest, runtime service bundle, worker environment/options, company config rows, database namespace, lifecycle and registration counts.
units.lifecycle: Discovers and executes manifest modules, installs packages into a shared directory, validates and persists them, applies migrations, refreshes mutable local manifests, starts workers, replays company config, registers jobs/events/tools and performs best-effort teardown.
units.testAssessment: The focused auto-build suite ran 4 pure tests and skipped 5 embedded-PostgreSQL route tests. Other direct Loader coverage is distributed across still-separate inventory units; this source has no evidence for safe manifest evaluation, provenance, concurrent operations, refresh-policy equivalence, capability approval integrity or crash-consistent activation.
units.designRationale: Offer one operational entry point for local development and deployed plugins, keep install plus schema migration transactional, and make activation failure non-fatal to other plugins.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independently replaceable PackageSource, ManifestCodec, TrustPolicy, InstallationStore, MigrationRunner and RuntimeReconciler boundaries, with digest-bound approvals, short-lived credential projection and durable desired/observed state.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the install-row-plus-migration transaction, explicit activation result, runtime-service seam and full restart intent. Do not copy the loader wholesale; split authorities and use a declarative data manifest, staged content-addressed packages, sandboxed verification, realpath containment, per-installation locking, durable reconciliation and egress-aware credential leases.
units.responsibilityConflict: Discovery dynamically imports publisher-controlled JavaScript before validation; local refresh can bypass installation policy; raw multi-vendor API keys are forwarded under one coarse capability; proactive company scope follows config presence; upgrade and activation lack exact accountable approval/evidence and crash-safe state convergence.
evidence: 78f8c6c3 Recover managed bundled plugin workers on demand (#10429)

units.function: Pure and route-level regression fixtures for repository-bundled plugin auto-build, standalone dependency bootstrap, disable switches and manual recovery guidance.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises ensureLocalPluginBuilt directly and POST /plugins/install through Express with mocked lifecycle/activity/live events plus optional embedded PostgreSQL.
units.keyDataModels: Temporary package.json, paperclipPlugin entrypoints, generated manifest/worker/UI artifacts, admin actor and plugin registry row.
units.lifecycle: Creates fixture packages, optionally runs pnpm install/build, installs via the route, asserts artifacts and lifecycle calls, then removes temporary repository fixtures.
units.testAssessment: Four pure cases passed and five database-backed route cases skipped on this host. Coverage is useful for deterministic command selection but omits hostile scripts, symlink/path races, integrity, network isolation, timeout child cleanup, output limits, concurrent builds and partial rollback.
units.designRationale: Keep first-party source plugins runnable when dist or standalone runtime dependencies are absent while allowing operators to disable auto-build.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS development mode may need a trusted-source build convenience, but production installation must never turn an administrative package request into unbounded host code execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only as a development-profile test pattern with explicit trusted roots, immutable fixtures and no production package-manager execution. Add adversarial provenance, containment, timeout, concurrency and cleanup tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: The fixture admin triggers build and postinstall code without digest-bound approval, sandbox proof, accountable evidence or egress policy; the successful route cases were not executable locally.
